amazon-order.reveal_note: The real notice comes from amazon.com and sends you to your orders in the app. The fake comes from amaz0n-security.xyz, says your order is locked and wants payment details in 12 hours.
amazon-order.what_you_can_do: Don't click. Open the Amazon app or type amazon.com yourself and check Your Orders.

apple-id-locked.subject_label: An Apple ID alert, on your phone
apple-id-locked.reveal_note: The real alert comes from apple.com and tells you to go to account.apple.com yourself. The fake comes from apple-support-verify.top, says your Apple ID is locked and links to an unknown site.
apple-id-locked.what_you_can_do: Read the sender's address, not just the name. Go to account.apple.com yourself to check.

gift-card-request.reveal_note: The fake comes from a free webmail address instead of a company account, asks for gift cards (a classic irreversible-payment scam), and pressures secrecy -- a real request for a purchase goes through the normal expense process, never gift cards over email.
gift-card-request.what_you_can_do: Call or message Dana on a channel you already use. Real purchases go through expenses, never gift cards.

it-password-reset.reveal_note: The fake email's sender domain (meridian-it-helpdesk.com) isn't the company's real domain, and the threat of 'permanent suspension in 24 hours' is designed to make you click before you look closely.
it-password-reset.what_you_can_do: Don't click. Go to the IT portal yourself, or contact the Help Desk on a number you trust.

qr-parking-sticker.subject_label: A QR code at a car park
qr-parking-sticker.reveal_note: The real sign points to the Parking.sg app. The fake is a sticker, shouts PAY NOW, threatens a fine and prints park-sg-pay.top. A QR code never tells you where it leads.
red_flags: A sticker over the real sign
qr-parking-sticker.what_you_can_do: Never pay a fine from a QR sticker. Use the official Parking.sg app, and report the sticker.

singtel-hr-leave.subject_label: A Singtel HR email, on your phone
singtel-hr-leave.reveal_note: The real email comes from singtel.com, uses your name and tells you to open the HR portal from your own bookmark. The fake comes from singtel-hr-portal.top, threatens to cancel your leave and asks for your staff ID and password.
singtel-hr-leave.what_you_can_do: Read the sender's address before you act. HR never asks for your password; open the HR portal from your own bookmark.

sms-dbs-locked.reveal_note: The real text comes from the DBS sender name, carries no link and tells you to call the bank. The fake comes from a mobile number, says your account is locked and links to dbs-unlock.xyz.
sms-dbs-locked.what_you_can_do: Banks don't text you a link to unlock an account. Call the number on the back of your card.

sms-grab-prize.reveal_note: The real text is a plain trip update from the Grab sender name. The fake comes from a mobile number, says you won a prize and links to grab-win.top.
sms-grab-prize.what_you_can_do: You can't win a draw you didn't enter. Delete it, and check offers in the Grab app only.
